key_insight: Modern high-power, axially fed plasma torches could revive solution precursor plasma spraying (SPPS) by overcoming the narrow processing windows and low deposition rates associated with legacy hardware.
engineering_relevance: SPPS enables direct coating synthesis from dissolved metal salts, avoiding powder production while offering molecular-level composition control for complex oxides.
method: Inject dissolved metal salt precursors into a plasma jet to synthesize coatings.
Use high-power axial injection to improve thermal energy utilization and broaden processing windows.
Assess emerging axial SPPS results across diverse material systems.
evidence_signal: The perspective cites early laboratory demonstrations of practical deposition rates and coating microstructures and performance rivaling suspension plasma spray, but the abstract provides no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: Precursor handling, feedstock delivery, and process economics remain unresolved barriers requiring industrially oriented evaluation.
paper_title: Solution Precursor Plasma Spraying: Are We Missing a Trick by Dismissing It?
